notes: TRT uses ASC for Active Shallow Crust, SCC for Stable Continental Crust, SIF for Subduction Interface, and SIS for Intraslab and Deep Seismicity.

Comp. identifies C1, fault sources in active shallow crust; C2, distributed seismicity in active shallow crust; C3, fault sources in stable continental crust; C4, distributed seismicity in stable continental crust; C5, subduction interface; and C6, intraslab and deep seismicity.
Column N gives the number of sources in the inventory for each combination.

MFD identifies MFD1, a histogram of incremental annual occurrence rates in evenly spaced magnitude intervals (EvenlyDiscretizedMFD); MFD2, a sequence of MFDs of the same type associated with the nodes of a multi-point source (MultiMFD); MFD3, a truncated Gutenberg–Richter distribution (TruncatedGRMFD); MFD4, an explicit set of nonparametric ruptures with an occurrence-probability distribution associated with each rupture; and MFD5, a combination of seven MFD1 sources and two MFD3 sources at the subduction interface.

Mw min and Mw max give the bounds of moment magnitude; z min and z max give the depth bounds in kilometers. For C1–C4, z reports the extrema of the upper and lower seismogenic depths; for C6, it reports the extrema of hypocentral depth from the sample of up to 200 ruptures per source retained in the inventory. For C5, z was obtained from the three-dimensional nodes of the nine interface geometries.
